name: recruitment-receptor-blocked
title: Receptor realization: blocking the response abolishes recruitment

purpose.question:
In the receptor-level realization, if the activated response is forced off
(blocked=True, zeroing the activated-type chemotaxis lambda even for cells
that cross the receptor-occupancy activation threshold) while the cue is
still secreted, is recruitment abolished?

report.title: Receptor realization: blocking the response abolishes recruitment
report.objective: Repeat the receptor-recruitment world with the activated-type chemotaxis lambda forced to 0 (blocked=True, downstream of receptor binding) and measure the recruitment index over 500 MC sweeps across 5 seeds.
report.conclusion: Blocking the response downstream of receptor activation abolishes recruitment: the final recruitment index is 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467), below the 0.1 pass threshold, versus 0.5667 for the receptor-gated baseline, despite the cue being present and receptors still able to bind ligand (kd 2.9 nM, Nasser 2009).
report.main_insight: Blocking downstream of receptor occupancy — rather than blocking receptor binding itself — still abolishes recruitment, isolating the chemotactic response (not mere receptor activation) as the necessary cause even in the receptor-gated realization.
report.caveat: The response is now receptor-gated (emergent activation from a per-cell Hill relation), closing the phenomenological gap the phenomenological baseline flagged; the remaining gap is background-invariance -- the Kd calibration does not yet model adaptation to ambient cue levels, a future adaptive rung.

study_card.goal: negative control: response blocked downstream of receptor abolishes recruitment
study_card.mechanism: Identical receptor wiring to recruitment-receptor-baseline (per-cell Hill occupancy, kd 2.9 nM) except the activated-type chemotaxis lambda is forced to 0.
study_card.why_before_next: Isolates the receptor-gated response as a necessary cause, pairing with recruitment-receptor-baseline to establish the receptor arm's causal structure.
study_card.expected_result: Recruitment index stays below 0.1 for the whole run despite receptors still able to bind ligand.
study_card.main_expert_question: Does blocking downstream of receptor occupancy (rather than blocking binding itself) fully account for the loss of recruitment?

question:
In the receptor-level realization, if the activated response is forced off
(blocked=True, zeroing the activated-type chemotaxis lambda even for cells
that cross the receptor-occupancy activation threshold) while the cue is
still secreted, is recruitment abolished?
hypothesis:
With the cue present (rate 10) but the receptor-gated response disabled
(blocked=True), responders may still activate (naive -> activated) but no
longer chemotax, so the recruitment index stays near zero.
objective:
Repeat the receptor-recruitment world with blocked=True (the intervention)
and measure the recruitment index over 500 MC sweeps across 5 seeds.
description:
The intervention arm of the receptor-level realization, paired with
recruitment-receptor-baseline. The world and receptor wiring are identical
to the baseline -- same cue, same per-cell ReceptorSubcell computing Hill
occupancy against the same cited Kd (2.9 nM, Nasser et al. 2009) -- except
the activated type's chemotaxis lambda is forced to 0 in
chemotaxis_receptor.build_receptor_spec, the receptor-realization analogue
of pharmacologically blocking the response downstream of receptor binding.
As in the baseline, the Kd is recorded as a calibrated parameter
(model_settings below), not as a literature_target on the recruitment-index
test.
claim:
Blocking the response downstream of receptor activation abolishes
recruitment: the final recruitment index is 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467),
below the 0.1 pass threshold, despite the cue being present and receptors
still able to bind ligand.
expected_behavior: Recruitment index stays below 0.1 for the whole run.
Responders may still receptor-activate (naive -> activated) but do not chemotax, since the activated-type lambda is forced to 0.

readouts.name: Recruitment index
readouts.description:
Fraction of responder cell centres of mass within 15 px of the source
centroid; activated-type chemotaxis lambda is forced to 0 regardless of
receptor occupancy.

readouts.name: Mean approach
readouts.description: Fraction of the initial responder-to-source gap closed over the run.

readouts.name: Responder mean distance
readouts.description: Mean centre-of-mass distance from responders to the source centroid.

readouts.name: Receptor occupancy
readouts.description: Hill occupancy θ = c^h/(Kd^h + c^h) of the per-cell receptor at the local cue concentration; unaffected by the downstream block. Derived from the Hill law (ReceptorOccupancyLaw), not emitted per run.

readouts.name: Activation fraction
readouts.description: Fraction of responder cells whose occupancy crossed the activation threshold (naive→activated); activation still occurs even though chemotaxis is blocked downstream.

behavior_tests.name: Blocking the response abolishes recruitment (receptor realization)
behavior_tests.description:
Pass criterion: recruitment index below 0.1 at the end of the run.
Measured from workspace/chemotaxis_data/results/receptor_blocked.json
(5 seeds, [17, 29, 43, 61, 89]): recruitment index stays at 0.0 through
mcs 325, then drifts to 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467) by the end of the
run -- versus 0.5667 for the receptor baseline.

evidence.from_test: Blocking the response abolishes recruitment (receptor realization)
evidence.observed: recruitment index 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467) across 5 seeds despite the cue present and receptors still able to bind (baseline 0.5667)

findings.statement:
The intervention works in the receptor-level realization too: across 5
seeds the final recruitment index is 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467) with
the activated-type chemotaxis lambda forced to 0, versus 0.5667 for the
receptor baseline -- recruitment remains response-dependent even when
receptor binding itself is unaffected.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: Responders accumulate by adhesion differences, not receptor-gated chemotaxis.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: Unconfounded contact-J design (activated type-3 J-rows copied from naive type-2).
alternative_hypotheses.note: Adhesion is held equal across naive/activated, so only chemotaxis differs; irrelevant here since chemotaxis itself is blocked and recruitment still collapses.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: The recruitment signal is a metric artifact (spurious proximity counting).
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: Blocking the response abolishes recruitment (receptor realization)
alternative_hypotheses.note: Excluded by this arm itself — recruitment index falls to 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467), below the 0.1 pass threshold, when the response is blocked, versus 0.5667 for the receptor-gated baseline.

conclusion:
In the receptor-level realization, blocking the response downstream of
receptor occupancy (as opposed to blocking receptor binding itself)
abolishes recruitment, mirroring recruitment-inhibited's phenomenological
result. This isolates the chemotactic response -- not merely receptor
activation -- as the necessary cause, consistent with the baseline
investigation's finding for the phenomenological realization.

regression_compatibility.basis: Reproduces the expected abolished-recruitment behaviour with the declared energies, ICs, and Hill-occupancy wiring (activated-type lambda forced to 0).

biological_validation.basis: Recruitment index 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467) across 5 seeds, below the 0.1 pass threshold, versus 0.5667 for the receptor-gated baseline (kd 2.9 nM, Nasser 2009).

explanatory_gain.basis: Isolates the chemotactic response — not merely receptor activation — as the necessary cause, even in the receptor-gated realization.

biological_summary:
This is the response-blocked negative-control arm of the receptor-level
realization. The world and receptor wiring are identical to
recruitment-receptor-baseline — the same cue, the same per-cell
ReceptorSubcell computing Hill occupancy against the cited CXCL8-CXCR1
affinity (Kd = 2.9 nM, Nasser et al. 2009) — except the activated type's
chemotaxis lambda is forced to 0, the receptor-realization analogue of
pharmacologically blocking the response downstream of receptor binding.
Responders can still cross the receptor-occupancy activation threshold
(naive -> activated), but no longer chemotax. Across 5 seeds the final
recruitment index is 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467), below the 0.1 pass
threshold and far below the receptor-gated baseline's 0.5667 — showing the
chemotactic response itself, not merely receptor binding, is the necessary
ingredient for recruitment.

literature_anchors.expectation: Receptor occupancy follows a Hill law with Kd≈2.9 nM.
Blocking the chemotactic response downstream of receptor binding abolishes gradient-directed recruitment even when the cue is present and receptors can still bind.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Verified — observed value matches (0.0667 vs 0.5667 baseline)

key_assumptions: Same world geometry and receptor wiring as recruitment-receptor-baseline; only the activated-type chemotaxis lambda is forced to 0.
Responders can still cross the receptor-occupancy activation threshold (naive -> activated); blocked=True acts downstream of receptor binding, not on it.
Recruitment radius = 15 px, identical to recruitment-receptor-baseline.

model_change.notes:
Same receptor-gated CPMProcess as recruitment-receptor-baseline, with the
activated-type chemotaxis lambda forced to 0 (blocked=True) in
chemotaxis_receptor.build_receptor_spec while cue_rate and kd are
unchanged. Receptor occupancy computation and the naive->activated switch
are unaffected — only the downstream chemotactic response is blocked. No
new state variables or listeners were added.

design_pivot_required.question: Should the receptor-realization's response-blocked condition be built as a dedicated study arm, or treated only as an implicit lambda=0 comparison?
alternatives: Treat blocked=True as an informal comparison only, folded into recruitment-receptor-baseline
Build a dedicated receptor-blocked study as a first-class necessary-ingredient control (this study)
design_pivot_required.notes:
Resolved by building this as its own study, mirroring recruitment-inhibited's
role for the phenomenological arm: it isolates the chemotactic response
as a necessary cause downstream of receptor occupancy, excluding "receptor
binding alone suffices" as an alternative explanation.
